decisions.reason: It builds directly on the firm's established waste-processing know-how and already shows a strong quantified customer benefit, so a growing firm with in-house R&D and research links is likely to retain and refine it rather than withdraw it.

As a product close to the core offer and still presented on its own page over two years, it fits the firm's absorptive capacity and service-based business well, even if public evidence of market traction is less explicit than for the modular plant concept.

This flagship modular line is central to the firm's stated direction, closely related to existing capabilities, and supported by a named customer case with substantial annual savings, making withdrawal very unlikely.

The new shredder line is close to the established product base and benefits from the firm's R&D and industry growth, but as a newer 2024 launch with limited visible outcome evidence it carries somewhat more risk than the proven 2023 concepts.

The spiral shaft screen line builds on existing screening and mobile system capabilities, so the firm can learn and improve it, yet as a fresh 2024 line without visible performance evidence it has the highest—though still modest—chance of being withdrawn.
